_about: Structured advising policies extracted from the CMPSC/DTSCE handbook PDFs by backend/data/policy_extractor.py. `scope` matches classify_major() and `topic` matches detect_question_intent(), so policy_service.py can relay them by intent without a retrieval step. Regenerate whenever the handbook PDFs change: python -m backend.data.policy_extractor

policies.title: Entrance to Major Requirements
policies.statement: Due to over enrollment, the computer science and computer engineering majors are controlled majors. This means for entrance to the major you must successfully complete the required ETM courses AND you must have the needed minimum cumulative GPA for your ETM year when you are in the ETM credit window specified in the Bulletin.

policies.title: Transfer and Change of Major Restrictions
policies.statement: The CSE Department will not approve requests for transfers from other colleges and universities, requests for change of major after a student has been admitted to a major, requests for computer engineering or science as a second (or later) concurrent major, nor for either major as a sequential major.

policies.title: Transfer Course Restrictions
policies.statement: Note that CMPSC 473, CMPSC 461, CMPSC 464, CMPSC 465 and the writing courses (CMPSC 431W or CMPSC 483W) must be taken at Penn State.

policies.title: Transfer Credit Approval
policies.statement: If you hope to use a transfer course that you have not taken yet to replace a CMPSC or CMPEN course, email a copy of the course syllabus to the Department Associate Head, Professor John Hannan (jjh9@psu.edu) before enrolling in the course to check whether it will be allowed to count for that requirement.
details: If Professor Hannan approves the use of the transfer credit, you will then need to fill out a petition at https://coursesub.psu.edu/ to have the transfer credit count correctly on your degree audit.

policies.title: Contact for Non-Advising Issues
policies.statement: For non-advising issues (questions about e-petition status, course controls, etc.) see one of the CSE staff in W209 Westgate during regular business hours.

policies.title: 400-Level CMPSC/CMPEN Course Selection
policies.statement: Select 3 credits from any 400-level CMPSC or CMPEN course, excluding 494, 495, 496, 499 and courses offered at non-UP locations which cover duplicate material (unless prior approval has been given for you to use a CMPSC or CMPEN 499 course).
details: The course you use for this requirement cannot double count with any other requirement for the CMPSC major.
Check with your advisor before planning on taking CMPSC 497 or CMPEN 497 for this requirement.

policies.title: Course Credit Limitation for CMPSC/MATH 451 and CMPSC/MATH 455
policies.statement: You may not use both CMPSC/MATH 451 and CMPSC/MATH 455 toward degree requirements.

policies.title: Department List (General Elective) Guidelines
policies.statement: Choose enough credits to bring the total number of credits up to at least 127.
details: At least 127 total credits required.
No courses not satisfying minimum requirements for baccalaureate degree program.
No courses described as intended for non-science or non-technical majors in the course description in the Bulletin.
No courses similar or remedial to a required course or course already taken.
Not ENGL 4, 5, or any other remedial English.
No more than 3 additional credits of physical education.
No more than 3 credits of Cooperative Education.
No more than 2 credits of Engineering Internship.
No more than 3 credits of CHEM 106.

policies.title: Department List (General Elective) Restrictions
policies.statement: The following courses are not eligible for the department list requirement: Astronomy (ASTRO) 1, 6, 7N, 10, 11, 120, 140; Biological Science (BISC) 1, 2, 3, 4; Chemistry (CHEM) 1, 3, 101, 108; Communication Arts and Sciences (CAS) 126, 283; Computer Science (CMPSC) 100, 101, 200, 201, 203; Cybersecurity Analytics and Operations (CYBER) 100; Earth and Mineral Sciences (EMSC) 150; Electrical Engineering (EE) 465; English as a Second Language (ESL) 4; Information Science & Technology (IST) 140, 210, 220, 230, 240, 242, 261, 311, 361; Language and Literacy Education (LLED) 5, 10; Mathematics (MATH) 200, 201, MATH below 140; Philosophy (PHIL) 12; Physical Science (PHSC) 7; Physics (PHYS) 250, 251, PHYS below 211; Science, Technology, and Society (STS) 150; Statistics (STAT) below 318 except for STAT 200; Statistics (STAT) 401, 487; STAT (MATH) 318, STAT (MATH) 319, STAT (MATH) 414, STAT (MATH) 415, STAT (MATH) 418.

policies.title: Foreign Language Proficiency Requirement
policies.statement: CMPSC majors are required to demonstrate proficiency equivalent to two semesters of a single foreign language.
details: Complete the 4th or higher year of a single foreign language in high school and submit a petition with your high school transcript.
Complete the 2nd (or higher) semester of one foreign language.
Complete two semesters (8 credits) of a NEW foreign language.
Successfully complete Penn State’s proficiency testing in a foreign language.

policies.title: Supporting Courses Requirement
policies.statement: Choose six credits of 400-level non-CMPSC/CMPEN/DS courses, having a common theme, that support a career in computer science.
details: Independent study credits may not be used.
Using any course that does not automatically count on your audit as a supporting course requires a petition at https://coursesub.psu.edu/.
Most approved 400-level Math classes will automatically count as supporting courses on your degree audit.

policies.title: Petition for Course Substitution
policies.statement: If you hope to use a course in a way that it does not automatically fill in on your audit, you must submit a petition at https://coursesub.psu.edu/ so that it can be determined whether the substitution you are requesting will be permitted and, if so, your degree audit can be updated.
details: Submit course substitution petitions prior to taking courses and prior to the semester in which you plan to graduate.
Petitions that require College level approval must be submitted BEFORE the semester in which you plan to graduate.

policies.title: Advising for Students Intending to Major in Computer Science
policies.statement: If you are a student at University Park who is intending to major in computer science but who has not yet officially entered the major, you can make an appointment through Starfish to meet with an adviser at the Engineering Advising Center (EAC), 208 Hammond Building, 863-1033.

policies.title: Advising for Students Who Have Entered the Major
policies.statement: If you are a student who has officially entered the computer science major, you can find your assigned adviser’s name and email address in LionPATH.
details: Always use your Penn State account for email communication.

policies.title: Cooperative Education Program
policies.statement: The cooperative education program provides work experience by alternating periods of academic study and full-time employment in industry or government.
details: The program typically starts at the beginning of the junior year and consists of three rotations, providing a cumulative work experience of one year.
Up to 3 credits of co-op may be used for your department list requirement.

policies.title: Internship Credit
policies.statement: If you prefer less of a time commitment, you can pursue one or more summer internships. You earn 1 credit per internship (maximum of 2 credits total) that can be used for your department list requirement.

policies.title: Degree Audit Responsibility
policies.statement: The final responsibility for selecting courses and meeting degree requirements is yours. You must have your degree audit reviewed by your advisor periodically.

policies.title: First Year Seminar Requirement
policies.statement: Most CMPSC majors take a 1-credit first-year seminar in either their first or second semester at Penn State.
details: If you did not take a first-year seminar that was a separate 1-credit course, you must make up the first-year seminar credit by taking an extra credit of coursework that is acceptable for the department list requirement.
Submit a petition at https://coursesub.psu.edu/ requesting to use the extra credit of department list coursework to fulfill the first-year seminar requirement on your degree audit.

policies.title: Graduation Requirements
policies.statement: To graduate from the University, every student must: (1) Complete the course requirements for his or her major (including earning Cs or higher in all C-required courses) and (2) Earn at least a 2.0 cumulative grade-point average for all courses taken at the University.
details: Complete the course requirements for the major, earning Cs or higher in all C-required courses.
Earn at least a 2.0 cumulative GPA.

policies.title: Petition for Mis-Categorization
policies.statement: You should submit petitions to correct any mis-categorization by LionPATH. Failure to do so may result in delaying your graduation until degree requirements are met.

policies.title: C-requirements
policies.statement: Some courses for the major require a grade of C or higher to graduate.
details: Check your degree audit to see which classes require a grade of C or higher.
If a class is being used in a section of the degree audit that does not have a label about a C or higher being required, a D or above will fulfill that requirement.

policies.title: Concurrent Majors Policy
policies.statement: Concurrent majors will not be allowed in Computational Data Sciences and Computer Engineering or Computational Data Sciences and Computer Science, although it is possible to obtain a concurrent major with another non-enrollment-controlled program.

policies.title: Entrance to Major Requirements
policies.statement: For the entrance-to-major requirements, see the 'How to Get in' section of the Data Sciences major page in the University Bulletin for the year that you began at Penn State.
details: https://bulletins.psu.edu/undergraduate/archive/

policies.title: Transfer Course Syllabus Submission
policies.statement: If you hope to use a transfer course that you have not taken yet to replace a CMPSC, CMPEN, or DS course, email a copy of the course syllabus to CSE Associate Department Head Professor John Hannan (jjh9@psu.edu) before enrolling in the course to check whether it will be allowed to count for that requirement.

policies.title: Transfer Credit Approval
policies.statement: Before taking a course at another university, use the transfer credit tool in LionPATH and check with your adviser to be sure the course will transfer usefully.

policies.title: Advising Appointment for Intending Majors
policies.statement: If you are a student at University Park who is intending to major in Computational Data Sciences but who has not yet officially entered the major, you can make an appointment through Starfish to meet with an adviser at the Engineering Advising Center (EAC), 208 Hammond Building, 863-1033.

policies.title: Assigned Adviser for Official Majors
policies.statement: If you are a student who has officially entered the DTSCE major, you can find your assigned adviser’s name and email address in LionPATH.

policies.title: Non-Advising Issues Contact
policies.statement: For non-advising issues (questions about e-petition status, course controls, etc.) see one of the CSE staff in W209 Westgate during regular business hours.

policies.title: Course Prerequisites Sequence
policies.statement: In particular, students should proceed through the Math 140 > Math 141 > Math 230 > Stat 414 > Stat 415 > CMPSC 448 > DS 340W sequence by taking the next course in the sequence each semester.

policies.title: Prerequisite Course Requirement
policies.statement: If a CMPEN or CMPSC course has prerequisites, you must complete the prerequisite course before taking the successor course.
details: For most courses an appropriate grade is a grade of D or higher.

policies.title: Prerequisite Override Requests
policies.statement: Prerequisite override requests are submitted through LionPATH.
details: For instructions about that process, see the document 'Requesting a Prerequisite Override' at https://lionpathsupport.psu.edu/student-help/.

policies.title: Petition for Course Substitution
policies.statement: If you hope to use a course in a way that it does not automatically fill in on your audit, you must submit a petition at https://coursesub.psu.edu/ so that it can be determined whether the substitution you are requesting will be permitted.
details: Be sure to submit course substitution petitions prior to taking courses and prior to the semester in which you plan to graduate.

policies.title: Petition Submission Deadline
policies.statement: Petitions that require College level approval must be submitted BEFORE the semester in which you plan to graduate.

policies.title: Course Registration Timing
policies.statement: At least several weeks before it is time to register for the next semester’s courses, refer to this handbook and consult with your adviser to determine an appropriate set of courses.
details: It is very important to schedule on your assigned scheduling date.

policies.title: Degree Audit Instructions
policies.statement: Instructions on how to run a degree audit are available at https://tutorials.lionpath.psu.edu/public/S_RunningDegreeAudit/.

policies.title: Degree Audit Responsibility
policies.statement: The final responsibility for selecting courses and meeting degree requirements is yours.

policies.title: Degree Audit Review
policies.statement: You must have your degree audit reviewed by your advisor periodically.

policies.title: What-If Reports Usage
policies.statement: Do not use a what-if report to check your degree requirements once you are in your major.

policies.title: Internship Credit

policies.title: Honors Program Thesis Requirement
policies.statement: Students in the Schreyer Honors College may earn honors in Computational Data Sciences by completing a thesis with a member of the CSE faculty.
details: See an honors adviser if you are interested in finding out more.
